standard.title: Household Sewing Machines — Flywheels — Specification (घरेलू सिलाई मशीनें — फ्लाईव्हील (गतिपालक चक्र) — विशिष्टि)
standard.description: This Indian Standard prescribes the material grade, dimensional requirements, tolerances, balancing criteria, surface finishing, and testing protocols for flywheels used in household sewing machines to ensure smooth rotational inertia, vibration-free operation, and perfect mechanical mating with the arm shaft and bobbin winder.
standard.scope: This Indian Standard prescribes the material grade, dimensional requirements, tolerances, balancing criteria, surface finishing, and testing protocols for flywheels used in household sewing machines to ensure smooth rotational inertia, vibration-free operation, and perfect mechanical mating with the arm shaft and bobbin winder.

certification.description: Voluntary Product Specification. Manufacturers are highly encouraged to obtain a valid BIS license to stamp or attach the physical ISI 'Standard Mark' directly on the packaging of the flywheel or the component itself to certify material grade, balancing, and plating quality in the competitive market.
requirements: Observed or calculated final test values, observed dimensions, or physical properties must be rounded off mathematically in accordance with IS 2:1960. The number of significant places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.
The flywheel must be cast using grey cast iron conforming to Grade FG 150 or FG 200 of IS 210, showing zero blow-holes, shrinkage cavities, cold shuts, or hard spots.
The casting must show a uniform Brinell hardness between 160 to 220 HB to ensure clean machining and prevent groove wear from drive belts.
The central hub bore designed to receive the flywheel bush (IS 13120) must be ground to a high-precision finish to prevent wobble.
Under Amendment No. 1, standardizes wheel diameters: outside rim diameter Ø 143 ± 1 mm, hub collar diameter Ø 74 ± 0.5 mm, and rim thickness width 19 ± 0.1 mm to control rotational momentum.
When mounted on a standard test mandrel, the lateral wobble of the side rim faces must not exceed 0.15 mm when rotated.
The radial eccentricity (run-out) of the outer rim must not exceed 0.12 mm when rotated on a test mandrel.
Every flywheel must be statically balanced. Any heavy side must be corrected by pocket-milling on the inner side of the web, ensuring smooth rotation.
The outer rim and hub face must be polished and given a bright, continuous nickel-chromium electroplated coating conforming to IS 1068, showing zero pinholes or peeling.
The recessed web portions of the flywheel must be thoroughly cleaned of grease and scale, primed, and finished with a glossy synthetic enamel paint or powder coating (typically black).
Under Amendment No. 1, a revised plating adhesion checking protocol is enforced, requiring the plating to resist scratching and show zero flaking under mandrel wrapping tests.
